2.text: wild reindeer becomes quite tame, and even comes to the train of the sledges.

3.text: After a while, however, it must be killed, and all the elements of the

4.text: incantation returned to their owners. The right-side reindeer is returned to

5.text: the Front Head. Meat puddings also are prepared with which to feed the

6.text: Winds. They are scattered (in crumbs) in all directions. The end.¹

7.text: Told by Aiñanwaˊt, a Reindeer Chukchee man of the Kolyma Country.

8.text: (b) When a wild reindeer-buck that has just shed his hair joins a domes-

9.text: ticated herd, the owner says, “Let us try it and make of him a tame reindeer!

10.text: Let him create offspring for us!” He goes to the herd and pronounces an

11.text: incantation. He talks to the Being of the Zenith. “Listen to me, you there

12.text: above! I am in great need. This one wants to go away, and he is the

13.text: first of his kind that I have seen here. Give me your wooden stake! I

14.text: will stick it into his foot and fasten him to the ground; I will thrust it in

15.text: between his antlers; I will pierce his lower jaw, and bring it down to the

16.text: level of the ground. With what else will I pin to the ground this fleet-

17.text: footed reindeer-buck? I will gather bowlders from all sides, and pile them

18.text: up between his antlers. How will he move his head? I will wrap his ears

19.text: with sod. I will gather withered sedge-grass and cover his nose with it.

20.text: Let all bad odors from every part of the earth enter into his nose! I make

21.text: him into a fawn newly born. O Vaˊɪrg̣ɪn! do not despise my demand. Let

22.text: me get possession of him! I will give you in exchange something equally

23.text: worthy of desire.” Then he spits, to fasten the incantation. After that he

24.text: says, “Bring the herd to the house!” The wild buck is very tame. They drive

25.text: the herd windward, so that he will smell the odor of the house, and hear the

26.text: noise of the people. But he is heavy, and less shy than before. The end.

27.text: Told by Keᵋuteˊhɪn (man) on the Oˊnmɪlɪn Tundra, 1901.

28.text: 2. INCANTATION USED ON THE MIDDLE ANADYR IN HUNTING WILD REINDEER.

29.text: I call every game, every living thing, from the very first limit of creation.

30.text: A young pintail duck I use for my leader, it is so clever in hiding from

31.text: everybody. I call an old pintail duck to be my leader. The lone reindeer-

32.text: buck I make to wade into the water. Oh! let us try to adopt it for the

33.text: leader! Let him give his call before the reindeer! Now I sing, “Just so,

34.text: just so! Oh! who are you?” I use the distance (to the game) of yesterday,

35.text: I use the distance of to-day. I make them appear before me! I cover my

36.text: face with the soot; to every kind of game I become unknown; to every

37.text: species of animal I become unrecognizable. Only the soot of my face appears
